references.text: Joseph informs Pharaoh that his father and brothers have come from Canaan with their livestock and all they own – the direct context for the presentation of the brothers.
Joseph prepares his brothers for their meeting with Pharaoh and advises them on what to say, setting the stage for the presentation in 47:2.
Pharaoh asks the brothers about their occupation, and they answer that they are shepherds – this is the direct continuation of the presentation in verse 2.
Stephen refers to Joseph's family becoming known to Pharaoh, reflecting the presentation of the brothers in Gen 47:2.
Part-whole relationship: the presentation of five brothers is part of the total migration of the entire clan.
Clear contrast in Pharaoh's role: expulsion of Abraham versus reception of Joseph's family.
Direct narrative sequence: the reunion (45:15) leads directly to the presentation before Pharaoh (47:2).
